Subject: Pilot sizing question — warmup + commitment tiers

Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow-up from our infra team: we run a mix of synchronous chat endpoints and async batch summarization. We're trying to map your Dedicated commitments to expected p95 latency and tokens/sec for our workload. Two specifics:

- Cold-start / model warmup costs for long contexts (14k tokens) — how much headroom should we budget?
- If we do a tiered reserve (Small/Medium/Large) for pilot scaling over Q4, how do tokens/sec translate to A100/H100 slab sizing?

Can you share a conservative tokens/sec estimate per slab (and recommended buffer) plus any caveats around KV cache warmup?

Appreciate it — happy to loop Alex (infra) in.

— Julia
Senior Infra, SkyTrail AI

[No attachments]

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Julia Morris <julia@skytrail.ai>, Alex Chen <alex@skytrail.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-03T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — warmup + commitment tiers

Julia — thanks, good questions. I summarized our back-of-envelope pilot sizing and attached the model. High level first, then numbers.

TL;DR
- For chat with 4k average response length and 14k context cold-starts, budget ~30–40% headroom above steady-state TPS to cover warmup + p95 SLOs.
- On H100: a single 80GB H100 slab (quantized FP16 path) supports ~550–700 tokens/sec for your benchmarked model (chat config). On A100 40GB: ~320–420 tokens/sec.
- Recommend a 3-tier pilot: Small (2x A100), Medium (1x H100 + 2x A100), Large (3x H100) with burst buffer + prefix cache sizing in the model.

Notes and caveats
- Cold-starts: KV cache warmup for a 14k context is the dominant latency spike on first request chain — expect p95 multiples of steady-state until cache warms across the slab (typically 20–80 requests depending on request pattern). We model warmup as a 30–40% effective throughput drag for the first 30m of steady traffic in conservative scenarios.
- Quantization: our numbers assume Q8/FP16 hybrid kernels we recommend for your model; using INT8 or more aggressive quant reduces token cost but may increase tail latency for certain ops.
- Batching and concurrency: continuous batching amplifies slab efficiency — we assume typical concurrency 8–12 for chat endpoints. If you expect low concurrency (<4), add 15% more slabs.

I've attached the spreadsheet (skytrail-warmup-model.xlsx) with per-slab tokens/sec, expected p95 tail, and a slot-efficiency sheet. Ben — can you confirm the H100 math matches our kernel profiling?

Next steps
- Ben to confirm microbenchmarks
- Karthik to map to tiered pricing and recommended commit sizes
- If that looks good, we set a 4-week pilot with Medium tier and a 20% burst reserve.

Best,
Irene Choi\Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference\irene@redwood.com

Attachment: skytrail-warmup-model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 84KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, Julia Morris <julia@skytrail.ai>

Date: 2026-09-04T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — warmup + commitment tiers

Adding the microbench detail from kernel profiling (pasted from our lab runs):

Bench assumptions:
- Model: open-encoder-base equivalent (instruction-tuned)
- Context: 14k tokens (priming + conversation)
- Response: 2k tokens average per inference (post-tokenization) for summarization; chat responses ~600 tokens avg in pilot flows
- Hardware: H100 80GB NVL, A100 40GB, quant path hybrid FP16/Q8 where appropriate

Measured tokens/sec (steady-state, median):
- H100 (80GB): 630 t/s (median), p95 latency at this throughput ~220ms/token. Conservative production estimate: 550 t/s.
- A100 (40GB): 370 t/s (median), p95 latency ~310ms/token. Conservative estimate: 320 t/s.

Warmup and tail modeling:
- First request chain (empty KV cache) increases per-token latency by ~1.6x on H100 and ~1.8x on A100 for early requests that trigger many attention recomputations.
- We model effective throughput during warmup window as 60–70% of steady-state depending on request hit patterns. Put another way, system needs additional capacity equal to ~35% of committed slabs to keep p95 SLO during warmup events.

Tier mapping (recommended conservative config):
- Small pilot (non-critical): 2 x A100 → steady ~640 t/s conservatively, recommended commit Slack: +35% → effective safety floor ~420 t/s available for spikes.
- Medium (recommended initial pilot): 1 x H100 + 2 x A100 → steady ~1,300 t/s conservatively, safety floor w/ warmup buffer ~845 t/s.
- Large (production posture): 3 x H100 → steady ~1,650 t/s, safety floor ~1,072 t/s.

Burst policy:
- Suggest 25% burst capacity above committed slabs for the pilot gated by auto-fallback to hosted variants if sustained >10m.

I'll attach the slot-efficiency heatmap (slot-efficiency-heatmap.pdf) that shows per-traffic-shape utilization. This lines up with Irene's spreadsheet.

Ben Carter\Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference\ben@redwood.com

Attachment: slot-efficiency-heatmap.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — warmup + commitment tiers

Julia / Alex — thanks for the patience. Recap and an operational playbook for the pilot below.

Recap (concise)
- Medium pilot (1 H100 + 2 A100) is our recommended starting point for your mix of chat + batch with large contexts. Conservative steady tokens/sec ~1,300 t/s; plan for ~35–40% extra capacity to maintain p95 during KV-warmup windows.
- For peak protection, enable a burst policy of +25% capacity for short spikes and Auto-Fallback to hosted slim variants for sustained >10m overload.
- Expect cold-start tail for first large-context chains — mitigated by prefix caching (warm up known prompts) and client-side warmup probes in the first 5–10 minutes after deployment.

Operational playbook (first 6 weeks)
1) Week 0 — Provision Medium tier, enable prefix caching for top 10 prompts, configure burst + fallback.
2) Week 1–2 — Load run: simulate 500–1,500 concurrent users with scheduled cold-start waves; measure p95 and KV-hit ratio.
3) Week 2–4 — Adjust commit (scale to Large if sustained >70% utilization), test rollback policies and DocuSign for expanded commit if needed.
4) Ongoing — Quarterly re-eval of model quantization profile vs cost.

Action items
- Karthik: I'll hand over the tier & pricing recommendation draft for the deal (will include the 4-week pilot offer with Medium commit + 25% burst).
- Julia / Alex: Confirm whether you want us to run the synthetic warmup load during Week 1 (we can run it on your Thursday maintenance window).
- Laura: I'll loop CS for onboarding notes / escalation path for the pilot.

If you want, we can schedule a short 30-min call next week to walk the spreadsheet and heatmap.

Best,
Irene\Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference\irene@redwood.com
